Corsican

[edit]
Corsican Wikipedia has an article on:
volpe
Wikipedia co

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • vorpe, volpi, vulpi

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin vulpes, from Proto-Italic *wolpis, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wl(o)p. Cognates include Italian volpe and Romanian vulpe.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈvolpe/

Noun

[edit]

volpe f (plural volpi)

  1. fox (Vulpes vulpes)
    Synonyms: mammacara, codipinnacciuta, codilonga
  2. (figurative) a malicious person

References

[edit]
  • “volpe, vorpe, volpi, vulpi” in INFCOR: Banca di dati di a lingua corsa

Galician

[edit]

Noun

volpe m (plural volpes)

  1. fox

  • “volpe”, in Dicionário Estraviz de galego (in Galician), 2014–2026

Italian

[edit]
Italian Wikipedia has an article on:
volpe
Wikipedia it

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • golpe (Tuscan)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin vulpēs (accusative vulpem) from earlier volpēs, from Proto-Italic *wolpis, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wl(o)p ~ *h₂ulp (“(red) fox”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈvol.pe/
  • Rhymes: -olpe
  • Hyphenation: vól‧pe
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

volpe f (plural volpi, diminutive volpétta or volpìna or volpìno m or volpicèlla or volpicìno m, augmentative volpóna or volpóne m, diminutive-augmentative volpacchiòtta or volpacchiòtto, pejorative volpàccia; (always figurative) volponàccia or volponàccio m)

  1. fox, vixen
  2. a crafty person

Derived terms

[edit]
  • volpacchiotto
  • volpeggiare
  • volpicino
  • volpino
  • volpone

Further reading

[edit]
  • volpe in Collins Italian-English Dictionary
  • volpe in Luciano Canepari, Dizionario di Pronuncia Italiana (DiPI)
  • volpe in garzantilinguistica.it – Garzanti Linguistica, De Agostini Scuola Spa
  • vólpe in Dizionario Italiano Olivetti, Olivetti Media Communication

Anagrams

[edit]
  • polve

[edit]

  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈwɔɫ.pɛ]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈvɔl.pe]

Noun

volpe

  1. ablative singular of volpēs
